intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Milford Sound, Fiordland National Park Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle through the stunning fiords of Milford Sound, exploring sea caves, waterfalls, and dramatic coastal cliffs. Get up close to fur seals and dolphins while surrounded by towering peaks meeting the Tasman Sea. A perfect blend of hiking access and beachfront adventure.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge near Queenstown. Operated by AJ Hackett, the original pioneers of commercial bungee jumping, this adrenaline-fueled leap offers breathtaking views of the surrounding alpine landscape and is a bucket-list must for thrill-seekers.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Hike along the golden sandy beaches and turquoise bays of the Abel Tasman National Park coastal track. This iconic beachfront trail winds through native bush, past secluded coves, and along pristine shorelines. Combine with a water taxi return for a perfect full-day coastal adventure.

experiences.name: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maori culture with a traditional hangi meal cooked underground using heated stones. Enjoy powerful haka performances, waiata (songs), and storytelling by the shores of the region. Learn about the rich indigenous heritage of the South Island while savoring slow-cooked lamb, kumara, and vegetables.

experiences.name: Kaikoura Seafood and Coastal Dining Experience
experiences.description: Indulge in the freshest crayfish (rock lobster) and seafood chowder at the famous Kaikoura Seafood BBQ stall right on the beachfront. Pair your meal with locally sourced green-lipped mussels and sauvignon blanc while watching fur seals bask on nearby rocks. A quintessential South Island food experience by the sea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Milford Sound, Fiordland National Park Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Christchurch International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs and collect luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into budget accommodation in Christchurch (hostel like Haka House or YHA Christchurch). Take a free self-guided walk through the Christchurch Botanic Gardens and explore the colourful street art of the Re:START container mall area in the city centre.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Avon River precinct and visit the free Cardboard Cathedral to appreciate post-earthquake resilience. Grab dinner at a local food truck or night market if available.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Pick up a cheap sandwich or pie from a New World or Countdown supermarket near the city centre (~NZD $5–8)
meals.dinner: Burger & beers at Pomeroys Old Brewery Inn or a cheap kebab/fish & chips from a local takeaway (~NZD $10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Book a budget hostel dorm in Christchurch in advance (YHA or Haka House ~NZD $30–40/night). Get an NZ SIM card at the airport (2degrees or Skinny Mobile are cheapest). Begin planning your hire car — picking up tomorrow morning is ideal for the South Island road trip.

day_by_day.morning: Pick up a budget hire car from Christchurch (compare rates on Rentals.co.nz — aim for ~NZD $40–60/day). Drive south on SH1 toward Lake Tekapo (~3.5 hours). Stop at Geraldine village for a quick stretch and visit the free Giant Jersey (knitting art) and local craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Tekapo. Walk the short track to the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd (free, 15 minutes). Hike the Mt John Summit Track (2–3 hours return, free) for panoramic views of the turquoise lake and Southern Alps — one of the most spectacular free hikes on the South Island.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Lake Tekapo from the lakefront. Tekapo is a Dark Sky Reserve — stay up for world-class stargazing from the lakeside (free). Budget accommodation at Lake Tekapo YHA or Tailor Made Tekapo Backpackers (~NZD $35–45/night dorm).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at the Christchurch hostel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Christchurch supermarket eaten at Geraldine or roadside — saves money on the road (~NZD $5–8)
meals.dinner: Cook your own pasta or noodles in the hostel kitchen, or grab a cheap pizza from Tekapo's Four Square supermarket (~NZD $8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Fill up petrol in Christchurch before leaving — fuel is cheaper in the city. The Mt John hike is best done in afternoon light. Download the FreeRoam NZ app for free campsite locations along the route.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Lake Tekapo to Aoraki/Mt Cook National Park (~1 hour). Stop at Lake Pukaki viewpoint for the iconic turquoise glacier-fed lake with Mt Cook backdrop — completely free and unmissable. Begin the Hooker Valley Track (3 hours return, free) — New Zealand's most popular and accessible alpine hike, passing swing bridges and glacier lakes with direct views of Aoraki/Mt Cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Hooker Valley Track and reach the Hooker Glacier terminal lake. On the return, take a short detour to the Kea Point Track (2 hours return, free) for additional Mueller Glacier views if energy allows. Explore the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre visitor display (free entry to basic exhibits).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Twizel (~1 hour) for much cheaper accommodation. Stay at Twizel Holiday Park or Mackenzie Country Hotel (~NZD $25–35/night backpacker room). Relax and rest legs after a big hiking day.

meals.breakfast: Muesli bars and fruit eaten in the car en route to Mt Cook
meals.lunch: Packed sandwiches eaten at the Hooker Glacier lake — a stunning picnic spot
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal at Twizel holiday park kitchen, or cheap takeaway from Twizel's main street (~NZD $10–14)

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track requires no booking and no fee — just sturdy walking shoes. Weather in Mt Cook can change rapidly; pack a rain jacket regardless of forecast. Twizel is significantly cheaper for accommodation and food than Mt Cook village.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Twizel to Queenstown via the scenic Lindis Pass (SH8, ~2.5 hours). Stop at the Lindis Pass summit (free viewpoint) for sweeping tussock highland views. Arrive in Queenstown mid-morning and check into budget accommodation — Absoloot Hostel, Haka Lodge, or Base Backpackers (~NZD $30–45/night dorm).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the free Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2.5 hours return) for the best free panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range. Explore the Queenstown waterfront and lakefront gardens — completely free. Browse the lively Earnslaw Wharf area.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening — an immersive traditional Maori cultural experience with a hangi meal cooked underground using heated stones, accompanied by cultural performances, waiata (song), and haka. Book in advance as spaces are limited. This is a meaningful budget-friendly splurge for cultural depth.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Twizel before departure
meals.lunch: Fergburger is iconic but pricey — opt for a cheap pie or wrap from a Queenstown bakery or supermarket (~NZD $6–10)
meals.dinner: Included in the Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening experience — budget for the experience cost (~NZD $80–110 but includes full meal and cultural show)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Hangi Feast experience well in advance online. Queenstown is the most expensive town on the South Island — cook your own breakfasts and lunches to offset costs. The Queenstown Hill walk is completely free and rivals any paid viewpoint.

day_by_day.morning: BUNGEE JUMPING DAY! Head to the Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43m, the world's first commercial bungee site, ~NZD $165–185). Book the first morning jump slot for smaller crowds and great light. Watch others jump before your turn to build courage. The Kawarau Bridge is a historic landmark in its own right — free to watch from the viewing platform if you want to spectate only.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recover from the adrenaline rush with a free walk along the Kawarau Gorge. Drive to Arrowtown (~20 minutes from Queenstown) — a charming historic gold-rush village. Explore the free Chinese Settlement ruins, the Arrow River, and the cute main street. Walk the free Arrow River Bridges Trail (1.5 hours, flat and easy).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Watch the sunset over Lake Wakatipu from the waterfront — free and spectacular in November. Cook dinner at the hostel or grab cheap fish & chips lakeside.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen self-catered — oats, toast, eggs (~NZD $3–5)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Arrowtown — grab supplies from the Four Square supermarket there (~NZD $6–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or rice at hostel kitchen, or cheap fish & chips from a Queenstown takeaway (~NZD $10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bungy must be booked online in advance at bungy.co.nz — walk-ups are possible but risky in peak season. If budget is very tight, watching the bungy from the free viewing platform is still thrilling. Arrowtown's main street has free gold panning in the river — bring a pan or rent one cheaply.

day_by_day.morning: Do the Queenstown Bike Trail or walk the free Frankton Arm Walkway along the lake edge (2 hours, flat and scenic). Alternatively, hike the Ben Lomond Track partial route (free, steeper — go as far as the saddle for views, 3–4 hours return to saddle). Pack up and prepare for the drive toward Fiordland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Queenstown toward Te Anau (~2 hours via SH6). Stop at the free Kingston Flyer heritage railway site and Kingston lakefront for views of Lake Wakatipu's southern end. Arrive in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland. Check into Te Anau YHA or Barnyard Backpackers (~NZD $30–40/night dorm). Visit the free DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to plan your Milford Sound day.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the free Te Anau lakefront track at sunset — Lake Te Anau is New Zealand's largest South Island lake and the views are stunning. The town is quiet and relaxed — a good contrast to busy Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen self-catered in Queenstown before checkout
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Kingston or a roadside stop (~NZD $5–8 from supermarket)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel kitchen, or budget meal at The Sandfly Café or Miles Better Pies in Te Anau (~NZD $10–16)

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on groceries at the Te Anau Countdown/supermarket tonight — Milford Sound has very limited and expensive food options. Fill your petrol tank in Te Anau. Book your Milford Sound cruise in advance online for the best budget rates.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — drive the spectacular Milford Road (SH94, ~2 hours from Te Anau to Milford Sound). Stop at Mirror Lakes (free, 10-minute boardwalk), The Chasm waterfall walk (free, 20 minutes return), and the Homer Tunnel for photos. Arrive at Milford Sound and check into your Boutique Stay accommodation in Milford Sound, Fiordland National Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board a budget Milford Sound cruise (~NZD $45–75 for a 2-hour scenic cruise — Real Journeys or Go Orange are the main operators, book online for best prices). See Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, Bowen Falls, and spot fur seals and penguins. The scenery is genuinely one of the world's great natural wonders.
day_by_day.evening: After the cruise, walk the free Foreshore Walk along the Milford Sound wharf area. Watch the evening light on Mitre Peak from the waterfront — magical in November's long daylight. Enjoy your boutique stay accommodation — a well-earned upgrade after days of hostels.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the drive — muesli bars and thermos coffee in the car
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at The Chasm or Mirror Lakes during the drive — avoid the expensive Milford Sound Lodge café
meals.dinner: Self-catered or use boutique stay kitchen facilities; alternatively the Milford Sound Lodge Blue Duck Café for a treat (~NZD $18–25 mains)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the world's great scenic drives — allow extra time for stops. Check for road closures or avalanche warnings at milfordroad.co.nz before departing. November weather can include rain — Milford Sound actually looks spectacular in rain with hundreds of temporary waterfalls appearing on the cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning kayak on Milford Sound — Rosco's Milford Kayaks offers guided and freedom kayak hire (~NZD $85–120). Paddling at dawn before the cruise boats arrive gives you the fiord largely to yourself — an extraordinary experience. Alternatively, walk the free Key Summit Track partial route if returning to Te Anau direction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back along the Milford Road toward Te Anau, stopping at spots missed on the way in. Visit the free Lake Gunn Nature Walk (45 minutes, beautiful beech forest loop). Return to Te Anau for the night — re-check into YHA or Barnyard Backpackers.
day_by_day.evening: Optional: Book the Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour (~NZD $55–75) — a unique underground cave system with living glowworms, accessible only by boat. Book in advance through Real Journeys. Otherwise, enjoy a free sunset walk along the Te Anau lakefront.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at boutique stay before kayaking
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Lake Gunn or roadside — bring food from Milford Sound boutique stay supplies
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel, or try the Sandfly Café for a budget meal (~NZD $12–18)

day_by_day.notes: The glowworm caves are genuinely magical and different from Waitomo — worth the splurge if budget allows. Book both kayaking and glowworm caves well in advance as they sell out in November (peak season). The Lake Gunn walk is one of Fiordland's most underrated free experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau toward Dunedin via the Southern Scenic Route (SH94 to SH1, ~4.5 hours). Stop at Lumsden for a coffee break. Pass through Gore — the 'Country Music Capital of New Zealand' — for a quirky free photo stop at the giant brown trout sculpture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Dunedin early afternoon. Check into Hogwartz Backpackers or Manor House Backpackers (~NZD $28–38/night dorm). Walk the free Baldwin Street — the world's steepest residential street (Guinness record). Explore the free Dunedin Railway Station exterior (stunning Flemish Renaissance architecture).
day_by_day.evening: Walk the free Dunedin Octagon city centre area. Visit the free Toitu Otago Settlers Museum (open until 5pm) for New Zealand colonial history. Grab dinner in one of Dunedin's affordable student-area restaurants — the city has great budget food options thanks to Otago University.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel before the long drive
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a roadside stop or Gore (~NZD $5–8)
meals.dinner: Dunedin has great cheap eats — try Mazagran Espresso Bar area or a cheap student-friendly restaurant on George Street (~NZD $12–18)

day_by_day.notes: The Southern Scenic Route via Invercargill is an alternative and adds Bluff and the Catlins coastline — add a full extra day if you want to explore the Catlins (highly recommended for wildlife). Dunedin is a very affordable city — one of the budget-friendliest on the South Island.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the free Otago Peninsula (30 minutes from Dunedin city). Walk or drive to Sandfly Bay for a free encounter with wild New Zealand sea lions lounging on the beach — one of New Zealand's most accessible free wildlife experiences. Walk the short sand dune track down to the beach (30 minutes return).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Otago Peninsula to the free Taiaroa Head viewpoint. If budget allows, book the Royal Albatross Centre tour (~NZD $55) to see the world's only mainland royal albatross colony — genuinely world-class wildlife. Alternatively, watch albatrosses from the free public viewing area outside the centre. Return to Dunedin and visit the free Dunedin Public Art Gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Dunedin's vibrant café and bar scene — the city has a lively student culture. Visit the free Speight's Brewery exterior on Rattray Street (tours available ~NZD $30 if interested). Enjoy an affordable dinner in the student quarter.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel kitchen
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Sandfly Bay with sea lion views — one of New Zealand's best free picnic spots
meals.dinner: Dunedin's Countdown supermarket for self-catering, or cheap Thai/Indian restaurant on George Street (~NZD $13–18)

day_by_day.notes: Sea lion encounters at Sandfly Bay are completely free and genuinely extraordinary — keep 20m distance from animals as required by law. November is a great time as pups may be present. The Otago Peninsula road is narrow — drive carefully and allow extra time.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north from Dunedin toward Kaikoura (~3.5 hours via SH1). Stop at Moeraki Boulders (~NZD $5 parking fee) — extraordinary spherical boulders on the beach, a geological wonder. Walk the beach among the boulders (30 minutes). Continue north through Oamaru — stop for a quick free look at the Victorian Precinct's historic limestone buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kaikoura early afternoon. Check into Kaikoura Backpackers or Adelphi Lodge (~NZD $30–40/night dorm). Walk the free Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway (2.5–3 hours, spectacular coastal cliffs with fur seal colonies visible for free). See hundreds of fur seals up close at the free Ohau Point seal colony (15 minutes north of town on SH1).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the Kaikoura Peninsula with the Seaward Kaikoura Range as a backdrop — one of New Zealand's most dramatic landscape combinations of mountains meeting sea. Relax at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Dunedin hostel before early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Moeraki Boulders beach (~NZD $5–8 from supermarket)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Kaikoura hostel kitchen — buy fresh fish from the Kaikoura Seafood BBQ for a budget treat (~NZD $10–15 for a crayfish half or seafood chowder)

day_by_day.notes: The Moeraki Boulders are best at low tide — check tide times before visiting. Kaikoura is famous for whale watching (~NZD $145–180) — book if budget allows, or opt for the free seal encounters as a wildlife alternative. The Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway is completely free and one of the South Island's best coastal walks.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the Kaikoura Seafood and Coastal Dining Experience — visit the famous Kaikoura Seafood BBQ stall on the waterfront for the freshest crayfish (rock lobster) and seafood chowder. This is a Kaikoura institution and the most affordable way to enjoy the local seafood. Combine with a morning walk along the Kaikoura waterfront esplanade (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive north from Kaikoura toward Nelson (~3 hours via SH1). The coastal drive through the Kaikoura Ranges hugging the sea is spectacular. Stop at the free Clarence River mouth viewpoint. Arrive in Nelson — New Zealand's sunniest city. Check into Paradiso Backpackers or Nelson YHA (~NZD $30–40/night dorm). Walk the free Miyazu Japanese Garden in Nelson.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nelson's excellent free arts scene — the city has more artists per capita than anywhere in New Zealand. Walk the free Trafalgar Street arts precinct. Visit the free Nelson Provincial Museum (check closing time). Enjoy dinner at a Nelson restaurant or self-catered at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Kaikoura hostel
meals.lunch: Kaikoura Seafood BBQ — fresh crayfish half (~NZD $35–45) or seafood chowder (~NZD $10–15) — a budget splurge worth every cent for the freshness and setting
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Nelson hostel, or cheap pizza from Stefano's Pizzeria in Nelson (~NZD $15–20)

day_by_day.notes: The Kaikoura Seafood BBQ is a genuine highlight — even a seafood chowder cup is extraordinary value. Book whale watching in Kaikoura if you haven't yet — morning departures are best for calm seas. The drive from Kaikoura to Nelson is one of New Zealand's most scenic coastal routes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nelson — hike the free Centre of New Zealand Track (1 hour return) to the hilltop geodetic marker that was used as the survey point from which New Zealand was mapped. Panoramic views over Nelson, Tasman Bay, and the Richmond Ranges. Pack up and say goodbye to the South Island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Christchurch (~4.5 hours via SH6 and SH1 through the Wairau Valley and Marlborough wine country). Stop at a Marlborough winery for a free cellar door tasting (many wineries offer free tastings — Forrest Wines or Cloudy Bay visitor centre). Return the hire car in Christchurch with time to spare. Final supermarket run for snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening in Christchurch. Walk the free Margaret Mahy Family Playground and Avon River Precinct for a last look at the city's remarkable post-earthquake revival. Grab a farewell dinner at a Christchurch restaurant or takeaway before heading to airport accommodation or early check-in.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Nelson hostel — use up remaining food supplies
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in Marlborough wine country or at a roadside stop — or a cheap café in Blenheim (~NZD $8–12)
meals.dinner: Farewell meal in Christchurch — try Riverside Market food hall for affordable diverse options (~NZD $12–20), or self-catered from supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Return hire car with a full tank of petrol — fill up before the Christchurch city limit to avoid expensive station prices near the airport. Allow at least 30 minutes for hire car return paperwork. Check your flight departure time and allow 2–3 hours for airport check-in. Spend any remaining NZD on local food souvenirs — Whittaker's chocolate, Pic's peanut butter, and Kaikoura sea salt are great budget options.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Christchurch International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and pick up pre-booked rental car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Christchurch toward your first overnight stop. Head south along SH1 toward Lake Tekapo (approx. 3.5 hours). Stop at Rakaia Gorge lookout for a scenic break. Check in to a mid-range lodge in Lake Tekapo.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the shores of the strikingly turquoise Lake Tekapo. Visit the iconic Church of the Good Shepherd at dusk. Enjoy the clear night skies — Lake Tekapo is a UNESCO Dark Sky Reserve.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside café en route (e.g., Geraldine Bakery — try the famous pies)
meals.dinner: Mackenzie's Bar & Grill at Lake Tekapo — hearty New Zealand lamb or salmon dishes at mid-range prices (~NZD 30–45 per main)

day_by_day.notes: Book rental car in advance. Drive on the left in New Zealand. Lake Tekapo is an ideal first-night stop to break the long drive south. Confirm accommodation booking.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a short hike up Mount John (approx. 2 hours return) for panoramic views over Lake Tekapo and the Mackenzie Basin. The trail starts near the lakeside and rewards with stunning 360° vistas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to Queenstown (approx. 3.5 hours via SH8 through Twizel and Lake Pukaki). Stop at Lake Pukaki viewpoint for iconic Aoraki/Mount Cook reflections. Check in to your Queenstown mid-range accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant waterfront and Steamer Wharf area. Browse the lively town center and book your Nevis Bungy Jump for the following day.

meals.breakfast: Cowan's Café at Lake Tekapo — eggs, toast, and fresh coffee overlooking the lake
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Pukaki — grab supplies from a Twizel supermarket (sandwiches, fruit, local cheese)
meals.dinner: Fergburger, Queenstown — legendary local burger institution, mid-range pricing (~NZD 15–20). Expect a queue but worth it.

day_by_day.notes: Lake Pukaki viewpoint is best in morning light. Book Nevis Bungy Jump online through AJ Hackett — slots fill quickly in November (peak season).

day_by_day.morning: NEVIS BUNGY JUMP — Experience New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Transfer departs from AJ Hackett base in central Queenstown. The full experience including transfer takes approximately 3–4 hours. An absolute adrenaline highlight of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery time! Stroll along the Queenstown Bay waterfront or take a leisurely walk on the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (approx. 2 hours return) for sweeping views of the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Queenstown night scene. Visit the Skyline Gondola for sunset views over the lake and mountains (optional, ~NZD 35).

meals.breakfast: Vudu Café & Larder — wholesome breakfast bowls and great coffee before your big jump
meals.lunch: The Pub on Wharf — classic New Zealand pub fare, fish and chips or a hearty burger (~NZD 20–30)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant — mid-range fine dining with locally sourced South Island ingredients. Try the Canterbury lamb (~NZD 40–55 per main)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, secure clothing for the bungy. No loose items permitted. Minimum weight requirements apply. Adrenaline levels will be high — plan a relaxed afternoon. Book gondola tickets online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Te Anau (approx. 2 hours via SH6). Te Anau is the gateway town to Fiordland National Park. Stop at Kingston and the shores of Lake Wakatipu en route. Arrive and check in to a Te Anau guesthouse or motel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by boat tour (approx. 2.5 hours, book in advance with Real Journeys). Journey across Lake Te Anau and walk through ancient limestone caves filled with thousands of glowworms.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Te Anau lakefront at golden hour. Relax and prepare gear for the drive to Milford Sound tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Queenstown accommodation breakfast or a quick stop at a café before departure
meals.lunch: The Fat Duck Café, Te Anau — popular local café with great sandwiches and cabinet food (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Redcliff Café & Bar, Te Anau — cozy restaurant with local venison, lamb, and salmon dishes in a charming setting (~NZD 35–50 per main)

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau Glowworm Caves must be booked in advance — Real Journeys is the only operator. Afternoon departure tours are common. Stock up on groceries and supplies in Te Anau before heading to Milford Sound tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the spectacular Milford Road (SH94) from Te Anau to Milford Sound (approx. 2 hours). Stop at Mirror Lakes, Eglinton Valley, and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain. Walk through the Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound and check in to your Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: MILFORD SOUND COASTAL KAYAKING — Paddle through the stunning fiords, exploring sea caves, dramatic cliffs, and waterfalls. Guided half-day kayak tour with Rosco's Milford Kayaks (approx. 3–4 hours). Paddle beneath Stirling Falls and Lady Bowen Falls.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in to your boutique accommodation. Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Milford Sound at dusk — waterfalls illuminate in the fading light and the fiord turns glassy calm.

meals.breakfast: Prepare your own breakfast or grab supplies from Te Anau before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the kayak tour or a light meal at the Milford Sound Lodge café upon arrival
meals.dinner: Milford Sound Lodge Restaurant — the only dining option in the sound, serving hearty meals with local South Island produce. Expect mid-range to slightly higher pricing (~NZD 35–50 per main) given the remote location

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the world's most scenic drives — allow extra time for photo stops. Check avalanche and road closure updates before departure (especially after rain). Kayaking wetsuits and gear are provided. November is peak season — book kayaking well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Milford Sound cruise (depart 8:00 AM) — the sound is most magical at dawn before day-trippers arrive. Real Journeys or Cruise Milford offer 1.5–2 hour scenic cruises past waterfalls, Mitre Peak, and to the Tasman Sea entrance. Watch for dolphins, seals, and penguins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Key Summit Track from the Divide (approx. 3 hours return, drive back along Milford Road). Stunning alpine panoramas over the Hollyford, Greenstone, and Eglinton valleys. Alternatively, hike the Lake Marian Track for a dramatic glacial lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Milford Sound boutique accommodation. Relax on the deck listening to waterfalls and birdsong in total wilderness.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at accommodation before the early cruise departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the hike — prepare sandwiches and snacks the night before
meals.dinner: Milford Sound Lodge Restaurant — try the local blue cod or venison for your final evening in the fiord

day_by_day.notes: Book the morning cruise in advance. Sandflies are notorious at Milford Sound — bring strong insect repellent. The Key Summit Track is well-marked and suitable for moderate hikers. Pack rain gear regardless of forecast — Milford receives 7+ meters of rain annually.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Milford Sound after breakfast. Drive back along the Milford Road to Te Anau, then continue north toward Wanaka (approx. 4.5 hours total). Stop at the stunning Cardrona Valley viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Wanaka. Check in to mid-range accommodation. Take a walk to the iconic lone Wanaka Tree on the lakeshore (short, flat walk). Explore the charming lakeside town center.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along Lake Wanaka's waterfront promenade. The Wanaka Basin glows golden at dusk with views of the surrounding peaks.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Milford Sound Lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Mossburn or Lumsden — try a local café for a pie and coffee
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — beloved local Italian restaurant with wood-fired pizzas and pasta (~NZD 25–40). Booking recommended.

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Milford to Wanaka is long but scenic. Consider breaking the drive with a stop at Lake Hawea. Wanaka is a quieter, more relaxed alternative to Queenstown — enjoy the change of pace.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Roy's Peak Track from Wanaka (approx. 5–6 hours return, 16 km, 1,200m elevation gain). One of New Zealand's most iconic hikes with breathtaking panoramic views over Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring. Start early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Roy's Peak and return to Wanaka. Cool off with a swim at Wanaka Beach (the lake is refreshingly cold but swimmable in November). Rest and recover at accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka's café and bar scene. Visit Puzzling World for a quirky experience or browse local galleries.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Kika Wanaka — great eggs and smoothie bowls before the big hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Roy's Peak — essential as there are no facilities on the trail
meals.dinner: Ritual Café & Bar, Wanaka — relaxed dinner with local craft beers and New Zealand-inspired dishes (~NZD 30–45)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is CLOSED from October 1 to November 10 for lambing season. By November 22 it should be open — confirm with DOC before going. Start no later than 7:00 AM. Carry 2+ liters of water, sunscreen, and layers. This is a strenuous but rewarding day hike.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Wanaka north toward Nelson/Abel Tasman region (approx. 5.5–6 hours via Haast Pass and the West Coast). The Haast Pass road is one of the most dramatic drives in New Zealand — stop at Thunder Creek Falls and the Gates of Haast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north through Hokitika and Greymouth along the wild West Coast. Stop at Hokitika Gorge for the stunning turquoise water (short 30-min walk). Arrive in Nelson or Motueka area and check in to mid-range accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in to the Nelson/Motueka area. Explore Nelson's vibrant arts scene or relax after the long drive.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Wanaka before departure
meals.lunch: Hokitika — try Stumpers Bar & Café or pick up local whitebait fritters (a West Coast specialty)
meals.dinner: Hopgoods & Co, Nelson — celebrated Nelson restaurant with seasonal local produce and excellent wine list (~NZD 35–55 per main)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — start early. The Haast Pass road can be affected by weather and slips; check road conditions. Hokitika Gorge is a 30-minute detour well worth taking. Nelson is the sunniest city in New Zealand — enjoy the warmer climate.

day_by_day.morning: ABEL TASMAN COAST TRACK DAY HIKE — Take a water taxi from Marahau to Bark Bay or Awaroa (book with Abel Tasman Aqua Taxi). Hike back along the golden-sand coastal track through pristine forest, across swing bridges, and past turquoise bays. Approximately 4–5 hours hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking or relax on one of the stunning beaches along the track (Torrent Bay, Bark Bay). Swim in the crystal-clear water — November is perfect beach weather in Abel Tasman. Return by water taxi to Marahau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nelson/Motueka accommodation. Clean up and enjoy a relaxed evening in the region.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation or The Hooked on Marahau café before the water taxi
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — essential as there are no cafés on the track. Pack plenty of snacks and water.
meals.dinner: The Mussel Inn, Onekaka (if routing via Golden Bay) or Jester House Café near Motueka — relaxed garden setting with local mussels, craft beer, and New Zealand fare (~NZD 25–40)

day_by_day.notes: Water taxi must be booked in advance — Abel Tasman Aqua Taxi or Wilsons Abel Tasman are recommended operators. The track section from Bark Bay to Marahau is approximately 14 km. Tides affect some beach crossings — check tide charts with your water taxi operator. Sandflies present — bring repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Nelson south toward Kaikoura (approx. 3 hours via SH6 and the Marlborough wine region). Stop at Havelock for a green-lipped mussel chowder at The Mussel Pot restaurant — a must-do in the mussel capital of the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kaikoura. Check in to mid-range accommodation. Take the Peninsula Walkway (2.5–3 hours, easy-moderate) around the Kaikoura Peninsula — spot New Zealand fur seals lounging on rocks just meters away.
day_by_day.evening: KAIKOURA SEAFOOD AND COASTAL DINING EXPERIENCE — Indulge in the freshest crayfish (rock lobster) and seafood chowder at the famous Kaikoura Seafood BBQ (a roadside institution). Watch the sun set over the dramatic Seaward Kaikoura mountain range.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Nelson accommodation or a café en route
meals.lunch: The Mussel Pot, Havelock — steaming pot of green-lipped mussels in white wine and garlic (~NZD 25–30)
meals.dinner: Kaikoura Seafood BBQ — iconic roadside crayfish, paua fritters, and seafood chowder. Budget ~NZD 30–60 depending on crayfish size. The ultimate Kaikoura experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway is one of New Zealand's best coastal walks — do not miss it. Seals are wild animals — maintain a respectful distance (10+ meters). Crayfish at Kaikoura Seafood BBQ sells out — arrive before 5:00 PM. November is whale watching season — consider booking a Whale Watch Kaikoura tour if time permits.

day_by_day.morning: Optional: Early morning whale watching tour with Whale Watch Kaikoura (book in advance, departs 7:15 AM or 10:15 AM). Sperm whales are resident year-round; November also brings orcas, humpbacks, and dusky dolphins. Alternatively, join a dolphin swimming tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: HANGI FEAST AND MAORI CULTURAL EVENING PREPARATION — Drive north from Kaikoura toward Christchurch (approx. 2.5 hours). Check in to Christchurch accommodation. Explore the regenerating Christchurch city center — visit the Cardboard Cathedral and the Re:START container mall area.
day_by_day.evening: HANGI FEAST AND MAORI CULTURAL EVENING — Immerse yourself in authentic Maori culture with a traditional hangi meal cooked underground using heated stones. Experience poi, haka, and waiata (song) performances. Book through a local Christchurch Maori cultural operator.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Kaikoura accommodation before whale watch departure
meals.lunch: Café on the Way, Kaikoura or roadside stop — light lunch before the drive
meals.dinner: Traditional Hangi Feast — included in the Maori cultural evening experience. Expect slow-cooked lamb, pork, kumara (sweet potato), and vegetables with rich earthy flavors (~NZD 80–120 per person including cultural show)

day_by_day.notes: Whale Watch Kaikoura has a 95%+ sighting rate but offers a partial refund if no whales are seen. Book well in advance. The Hangi evening is a culturally significant and deeply memorable experience — approach with respect and openness. Confirm Christchurch Maori cultural operator bookings in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Christchurch. Visit the beautiful Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free entry) — stunning in November with spring flowers in full bloom. Walk along the Avon River through Hagley Park. Visit the Canterbury Museum (free entry) for South Island natural history and Maori taonga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return rental car at Christchurch Airport. Allow 2+ hours before departure for car return, check-in, and security. Browse duty-free for New Zealand souvenirs — Manuka honey, local wine, and merino wool products.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Christchurch. Reflect on 13 incredible days across the South Island — from the fiords of Milford Sound to the beaches of Abel Tasman, the adrenaline of the Nevis Bungy, and the warmth of Maori culture.

meals.breakfast: C1 Espresso, Christchurch — iconic local café in a heritage building with excellent coffee and brunch (~NZD 20–30)
meals.lunch: Little High Eatery, Christchurch — vibrant food hall with multiple vendors offering everything from sushi to gourmet burgers (~NZD 15–25)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car at least 3 hours before international departure. Christchurch Airport has good facilities for a final New Zealand meal and shopping. Ensure all biosecurity requirements are met — New Zealand has strict rules about bringing food items through customs. Kia ora and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Milford Sound, Fiordland National Park Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle through the stunning fiords of Milford Sound, exploring sea caves, waterfalls, and dramatic coastal cliffs. Get up close to fur seals and dolphins while surrounded by towering peaks meeting the Tasman Sea. A perfect blend of hiking access and beachfront adventure.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Experience New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge near Queenstown. Operated by AJ Hackett, the original pioneers of commercial bungee jumping, this adrenaline-fueled leap offers breathtaking views of the surrounding alpine landscape and is a bucket-list must for thrill-seekers.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Hike along the golden sandy beaches and turquoise bays of the Abel Tasman National Park coastal track. This iconic beachfront trail winds through native bush, past secluded coves, and along pristine shorelines. Combine with a water taxi return for a perfect full-day coastal adventure.

experiences.name: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in authentic Maori culture with a traditional hangi meal cooked underground using heated stones. Enjoy powerful haka performances, waiata (songs), and storytelling by the shores of the region. Learn about the rich indigenous heritage of the South Island while savoring slow-cooked lamb, kumara, and vegetables.

experiences.name: Kaikoura Seafood and Coastal Dining Experience
experiences.description: Indulge in the freshest crayfish (rock lobster) and seafood chowder at the famous Kaikoura Seafood BBQ stall right on the beachfront. Pair your meal with locally sourced green-lipped mussels and sauvignon blanc while watching fur seals bask on nearby rocks. A quintessential South Island food experience by the sea.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to boutique accommodation in Milford Sound, Fiordland National Park (approx. 4-hour scenic drive through stunning mountain passes and lakes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive through Te Anau and the Fiordland wilderness. Stop at Mirror Lakes and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain for photography. Check in to Boutique Stay in Milford Sound upon arrival (~17:00). Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink on the terrace overlooking the fiord.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive sunset cruise on Milford Sound aboard a private charter vessel. Watch the light fade over Mitre Peak with champagne and canapés. Return to lodge for a relaxed first night.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at Queenstown Airport's premium lounge
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch or stop at The Fat Duck in Te Anau for a quality café meal en route
meals.dinner: Private in-lodge dining experience — chef-prepared New Zealand lamb rack with local seasonal vegetables and Central Otago Pinot Noir

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep schedule light. Confirm private transfer booking in advance. Pack layers as Milford Sound weather can change rapidly even in November.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Coastal Kayaking — paddle through the iconic fiords, exploring hidden sea caves, bridal veil waterfalls including Lady Bowen Falls, and dramatic cliff faces. Guided premium small-group or private kayak tour departing at 08:00 for the calmest water conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from kayaking by midday. After lunch, embark on a guided walk along the Milford Track foreshore — explore the rainforest fringe, spot fur seals basking on rocks near the Milford Sound wharf, and enjoy interpretive commentary on Fiordland ecology.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing experience with a private guide — Fiordland is one of New Zealand's darkest sky regions. Enjoy hot cocoa and blankets on the lodge deck while learning southern hemisphere constellations.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the lodge — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch provided by the lodge during the kayak tour — artisan sandwiches, local cheese, fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: In-lodge dining: pan-seared blue cod with Fiordland greens, truffle mash, and a New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc from Marlborough

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking requires moderate fitness. Wear quick-dry clothing and apply reef-safe sunscreen. November weather in Milford Sound can include rain — embrace it as the waterfalls are more spectacular after rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day guided hike on a section of the world-famous Milford Track — depart early for the Glade Wharf to Clinton Valley section. Walk through ancient beech forest alongside the Clinton River with a private guide providing ecological and geological insights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking through the valley, spotting native birds including kea, tui, and fantails. Reach a scenic rest point for lunch before returning via the same trail or by private boat back to the Sound.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxation evening at the lodge — enjoy the outdoor hot tub with fiord views. Optional in-room massage treatment booked through the lodge's concierge wellness service.

meals.breakfast: Continental and hot breakfast at the lodge — freshly baked pastries, local honey, eggs to order, and pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch: charcuterie board, local brie, crackers, dried fruits, energy bars, and thermos of herbal tea
meals.dinner: Lodge dining: slow-braised venison with roasted root vegetables, red wine jus, and Otago Pinot Noir — followed by a pavlova dessert with fresh summer berries

day_by_day.notes: Ensure hiking boots are well broken in before this day. The Milford Track requires a permit and advance booking — arrange through the lodge concierge well in advance. Private guided access may bypass standard restrictions.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight over Fiordland National Park — soar above Mitre Peak, Doubtful Sound, and the remote Darran Mountains. Land on a remote glacier or alpine ridge for a champagne toast with panoramic views. A truly once-in-a-lifetime luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer departs Milford Sound heading toward Queenstown (approx. 4 hours). Stop at Lake Wakatipu lookout near Queenstown for photos. Check in to a luxury Queenstown property (e.g., Eichardt's Private Hotel or Matakauri Lodge) by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant lakefront. Pre-dinner cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables mountain range.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast before departure — smashed avocado, poached eggs, sourdough, and cold-pressed juice
meals.lunch: En route stop at a scenic lakeside café near Te Anau or Frankton — wood-fired pizza or gourmet burgers
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro, Queenstown — celebrated farm-to-table cuisine paired with award-winning Central Otago wines in a stunning vineyard setting

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are weather-dependent — have a backup activity plan. Book helicopter experience at least 2 weeks in advance. Queenstown hotel check-in should be confirmed ahead of travel.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — experience New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Private transfer to the Nevis platform via 4WD. Includes professional photography and video package to capture the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and recover with a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a scenic lakeside walk. Optional: wine tasting at a local Central Otago cellar door such as Peregrine Wines.
day_by_day.evening: Hangi Feast and Maori Cultural Evening — immerse yourself in authentic Maori culture with a traditional hangi meal cooked underground using heated stones. Enjoy cultural performances including haka, poi, and waiata (song).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full New Zealand spread with local cheeses, cold cuts, eggs, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Post-bungy celebration lunch at Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — modern New Zealand cuisine by celebrated chef Josh Emmett
meals.dinner: Hangi Feast — slow-cooked meats, kumara, vegetables, and rewena bread, accompanied by storytelling and cultural performance

day_by_day.notes: Bungy jumping has weight and health restrictions — check requirements in advance. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. The Nevis Bungy is operated by AJ Hackett and is considered very safe with world-class facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic jet boat ride on the Shotover River — carve through narrow canyons at high speed for an adrenaline-charged morning. Premium private charter option available for a more exclusive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Queenstown gondola ride to the summit of Bob's Peak. Explore the Skyline complex, enjoy luge rides, and take in 360-degree views of the Remarkables, Lake Wakatipu, and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Fine dining evening in Queenstown — enjoy a leisurely dinner at one of the town's top restaurants with stunning lake views.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivery at the hotel — eggs royale, fresh fruit platter, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Skyline Restaurant at the gondola summit — buffet with panoramic views, featuring New Zealand lamb, seafood, and local desserts
meals.dinner: Dinner at Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — premium New Zealand beef and lamb cuts, outstanding wine list, and a sophisticated alpine atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The gondola and luge are family-friendly but equally enjoyable for adults. Book the Shotover Jet in advance as it is extremely popular in November (peak summer season).

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic drive along the Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in New Zealand — through Arrowtown. Explore the historic Chinese settlement and gold-rush-era architecture. Visit local boutique galleries and artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north toward Wanaka (approx. 1 hour from Queenstown). Check in to a luxury Wanaka lodge (e.g., Minaret Station Alpine Lodge or Edgewater Resort). Afternoon kayaking or paddleboarding on the crystal-clear Lake Wanaka.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the iconic 'That Wanaka Tree' — the lone willow tree in Lake Wanaka, one of New Zealand's most photographed spots. Evening stroll along the lakefront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Queenstown before checkout
meals.lunch: Arrowtown lunch at The Chop Shop Food Merchants — gourmet burgers, local craft beer, and artisan sweets
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bistro Gentil, Wanaka — intimate fine dining with French-inspired New Zealand cuisine and an excellent wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is a highlight not to be rushed — allocate at least 2 hours. November is peak season in Wanaka; book accommodation and restaurants well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to Rob Roy Glacier Viewpoint in Mount Aspiring National Park — a stunning 10km return trail through ancient beech forest with dramatic views of hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and alpine meadows. Depart early with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from hike and enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the lodge. Optional: visit Puzzling World Wanaka for a quirky cultural detour, or enjoy a spa treatment at the lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Private wine tasting and dinner at Rippon Vineyard — one of the world's most beautifully situated wineries on the shores of Lake Wanaka, with biodynamic wines and stunning mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast — porridge with manuka honey, eggs, avocado toast, and coffee before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch in the Mount Aspiring backcountry — wraps, energy bars, fruit, and thermos of soup
meals.dinner: Rippon Vineyard private dinner experience — local meats, cheeses, and seasonal produce paired with estate Pinot Noir and Riesling

day_by_day.notes: Rob Roy Glacier Track is rated moderate — suitable for fit walkers. River crossing may be required; check conditions with your guide. November sees lush greenery and wildflowers along the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Wanaka toward the West Coast via the Haast Pass — one of New Zealand's most dramatic mountain highways. Stop at Thunder Creek Falls and the Gates of Haast for short walks and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the West Coast glaciers region. Check in to a luxury Franz Josef or Fox Glacier lodge. Helicopter flight onto Franz Josef Glacier with a guided ice walk — crampons and equipment provided.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the lodge after an exhilarating glacier experience. Enjoy the quiet rainforest surroundings unique to the West Coast.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast in Wanaka before departure
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside stop at a West Coast café — whitebait fritters (a West Coast specialty), fresh bread, and flat white coffee
meals.dinner: In-lodge or local fine dining — West Coast blue cod, green-lipped mussels, and local craft beer or Marlborough white wine

day_by_day.notes: Haast Pass drive is approximately 3-4 hours from Wanaka — depart by 09:00. Glacier helicopter flights are weather-dependent; have a backup glacier valley walk option. Whitebait fritters are a must-try West Coast delicacy.

day_by_day.morning: Guided rainforest walk in Westland Tai Poutini National Park — explore the ancient podocarp rainforest surrounding the glaciers, spotting native birds like kiwi (dawn walks), kea, and native pigeon (kereru). Visit Lake Matheson for the famous mirror reflection of Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer north along the West Coast toward Nelson/Marlborough region (long drive — consider breaking with a domestic flight from Hokitika to Nelson for comfort). Arrive and check in to a luxury Nelson or Marlborough property.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Marlborough wine region. Sunset walk through the vineyards of the Wairau Valley. Early evening rest after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at the West Coast lodge — local eggs, smoked salmon, toast, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Hokitika lunch stop — visit the famous Hokitika Gorge for a short walk and lunch at a local café with homemade pies and coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Marlborough winery restaurant — Cloudy Bay Cellar Door or Herzog Winery for world-class cuisine paired with estate Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The West Coast to Marlborough journey is long — a domestic flight from Hokitika to Nelson (Air New Zealand) is strongly recommended for a luxury itinerary. Book in advance. Herzog Winery restaurant requires reservations well ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Abel Tasman Coast Track Day Hike — depart from Marahau on the golden sandy beaches and turquoise bays of Abel Tasman National Park. Private guided hike along the coastal track with stops at Coquille Bay, Torrent Bay, and Bark Bay. Water taxi support available for a one-way hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Water taxi return from the trail endpoint back to Marahau. Afternoon at leisure — optional sea kayaking in the Abel Tasman marine reserve or swimming at a secluded golden beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Marlborough or Nelson accommodation. Relaxed evening with wine tasting at the lodge's private cellar.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Abel Tasman — granola, yoghurt, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed trail lunch on the Abel Tasman coast — artisan sandwiches, local brie, fruit, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Kaikoura Seafood and Coastal Dining Experience — indulge in the freshest crayfish (rock lobster) and seafood chowder at the famous Kaikoura Seafood BBQ (drive to Kaikoura for a memorable coastal dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Abel Tasman Coast Track is well-maintained and suitable for most fitness levels. Tides affect some beach sections — check tide times with your guide. The drive from Marlborough to Kaikoura for dinner is approx. 1.5 hours but absolutely worth it for the seafood.

day_by_day.morning: Kaikoura whale watching experience — board a luxury small-group vessel for a world-class sperm whale encounter. Kaikoura's unique underwater canyon makes it one of the best whale watching destinations on Earth. Dolphins, fur seals, and albatross are common sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kaikoura township — visit the seal colony at Point Kean, walk the Kaikoura Peninsula Walkway for dramatic coastal views, and browse local artisan shops. Optional: swimming with dusky dolphins experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer back to Christchurch (approx. 2.5 hours). Check in to a luxury Christchurch hotel (e.g., The George Hotel or Otahuna Lodge nearby). Celebratory farewell dinner in Christchurch.

meals.breakfast: Kaikoura hotel breakfast — eggs, local smoked fish, toast, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Kaikoura seafood lunch at Nin's Bin roadside crayfish caravan — fresh crayfish with lemon and butter, a legendary New Zealand experience
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The George Hotel's 50 Bistro, Christchurch — sophisticated New Zealand cuisine with Canterbury lamb, local wines, and impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching is weather and sea-condition dependent — Whale Watch Kaikoura offers refunds or rescheduling if conditions are unsafe. Book well in advance as it is extremely popular. Nin's Bin is cash-only and iconic — do not miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Christchurch. Explore the revitalized city center — visit the stunning Christchurch Botanic Gardens in full spring bloom (November), the Canterbury Museum, and the Re:START container mall. Optional: punting on the Avon River through the gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, visit the International Antarctic Centre for a unique New Zealand experience, or enjoy a final coffee and shopping in the city's boutique laneways. Private luxury transfer to Christchurch International Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Christchurch International Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day South Island journey.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast at The George — a final indulgent spread with local pastries, eggs, smoked salmon, and excellent coffee
meals.lunch: Christchurch farewell lunch at Gatherings Restaurant or Harlequin Public House — modern New Zealand cuisine with local craft beverages
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check out of hotel by 11:00. Store luggage with the concierge if exploring the city before afternoon departure. Confirm return flight details and allow 3 hours for international check-in at Christchurch Airport. Consider purchasing local souvenirs — Marlborough wine, manuka honey, and pounamu (greenstone) jewellery make excellent gifts.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
